title: MOOR Blueprint Farm — Master Production Architecture
page0: Create a Blueprint Farm inside MOOR: use the current Funnel to generate multiple extremely detailed end-to-end blueprints, preserve unanswered questions as open questions rather than prematurely solving them, reuse existing MOOR tools and verified machinery, choreograph future implementation into dependency-safe slices, make every blueprint inspectable in Pulse, and execute only the first infrastructure slice now. The farm must eventually be able to hand an approved blueprint to workers for build execution, but it must not auto-build future slices until explicitly selected.
correctedQuestion: What production system should MOOR use to continuously manufacture high-fidelity, evidence-backed blueprints from open questions, existing machinery, deterministic recipes and Funnel receipts, while keeping planning separate from execution and letting a human inspect, sequence and deliberately release implementation slices?
objective: Turn planning itself into cumulative production machinery: blueprints become versioned factory artifacts that can be inspected, compared, composed, re-run through the Funnel and later released to worker cells without losing intent or pretending uncertain decisions are settled.
coreLaws: Blueprint production and software execution are separate authority phases.
Every blueprint begins from immutable Page 0 and an explicit open-question inventory.
A blueprint may propose options, but an unanswered material question remains visibly unanswered until evidence, owner input or a lawful solver process resolves it.
Existing verified machinery is searched before new machinery is designed.
Reusable machinery is referenced by capability/contract/version, not copied as prose.
Deterministic generative assets prefer seed + recipe + generator version + parameters over storing every generated point.
Blueprints are immutable by version; revisions create lineage and supersession edges.
Every child blueprint carries dependencies, interfaces, acceptance, failure modes, maintenance burden, observability and rollback.
Implementation is released in slices whose prerequisites are already verified.
No slice may silently promote Ultra, bypass v44 production authority, or claim a documented component is wired/verified when it is not.
The 3D factory may visualize blueprint/workflow state, but the source of truth is machine-readable blueprint/receipt/maintenance data.
The farm accumulates knowledge: rejected options, failed assumptions and superseded blueprints remain searchable.

intakePipeline.purpose: Freeze the exact request and scope.
Attach current repository state, maintenance register, capability graph, manifest, prior blueprints, receipts, failures and owner evidence.
Generate questions whose answers materially affect architecture; do not encode an answer into the question.
Produce independent child blueprints around orthogonal problem surfaces.
Compare assumptions, interfaces, conflicts, duplicated responsibilities and missing dependencies.
Order implementation slices by dependency, risk, reversibility and information value.
Check all original obligations against the final blueprint family.
Issue traceable blueprint authority without authorizing unselected implementation.
Index the blueprint family in Pulse/Funnel Fabric for human and machine inspection.
Only an explicitly selected slice receives execution authorization and worker routing.

blueprintFamily.role: Remove theatrical/roundabout maintenance debt without weakening authority, fidelity or proven Funnel behavior.
Make the 3D physical machine a truthful, inspectable projection of software manufacturing state.
Let blueprints specify reproducible generated assets via seeds, recipes, generator capabilities and deterministic reconstruction.
Define the future worker/choreographer system that can execute selected slices without giving planners ambient authority.
Dependency graph, storyline and release plan across the full upgrade program.

toolDiscovery.selectionRule: Prefer the newest verified non-deprecated machine satisfying the required contract; preserve explicit lineage and use adapters instead of silent substitution.
toolDiscovery.generatorRule: For generative requirements, search for generators by outputs/capabilities first; if found, bind recipe/version/seed. Design a new generator only when no existing verified machine satisfies the needed output contract.

firstSlice.name: Blueprint Farm Registry + Pulse Library
scope: Create this blueprint family as versioned JSON artifacts.
Create a machine-readable Blueprint Farm index with dependencies, status and slice order.
Run the family through Ultra candidate Funnel for BlueprintReceipts while retaining v44 production authority.
Index the farm in Pulse Funnel Fabric / Learning Spine so other chats and future workers can discover it automatically.
Add regression checks that every indexed farm blueprint exists and carries open questions, maintenance, acceptance and slices.

doneCriteria: Five detailed child blueprints exist and are independently inspectable.
Every child blueprint contains genuinely open questions without solution-leading wording.
A choreography blueprint defines dependency-safe implementation slices.
Existing MOOR machinery is referenced rather than duplicated where it already satisfies a contract.
Blueprints distinguish verified existing state from proposed future state.
The Blueprint Farm is indexed in Pulse and Funnel Fabric.
The farm receives an Ultra candidate BlueprintReceipt family.
Only BF-01 is released/implemented now; later slices remain plans until explicit selection.

knownEvidence.claim: MOOR already has a mapped manufacturing model and quality law.
Pulse already has an inspectable Funnel Fabric library.
Ultra candidate can issue typed Blueprint/Execution receipts with native Page 0 replay.

openQuestions: What blueprint surfaces deserve their own child blueprint instead of remaining a section of another plan?
Which questions require owner judgment rather than solver evidence?
What is the minimum evidence package needed before a planned slice becomes eligible for release?
How should the farm compare competing blueprints without prematurely choosing one?
What blueprint metadata most helps future workers reuse existing machinery instead of inventing replacements?
How much planning detail improves execution quality before it becomes maintenance overhead?
Which blueprint changes should stale downstream slice eligibility?
How should blueprint lineage and supersession appear in the physical factory without suggesting planned work is already running?
assumptions: Production authority stays v44-sealed while Ultra remains candidate.
The repository and Pulse indexes are canonical evidence sources, not chat memory.
Planning artifacts can be useful before any worker automation exists.
Blueprints may be revised when new evidence invalidates assumptions.
nonGoals: Do not rebuild existing verified machinery merely to normalize naming.
Do not treat a detailed blueprint as proof of implementation.

interfaces.contract: Receive BlueprintReceipts; only an explicitly selected slice may receive execution authorization.
Resolve existing verified machinery before proposing new tools.
Release one exact slice packet only after authority/owner decision.

failureModes.containment: Status vocabulary separates specified-not-built from verified implementation.
Open-question checks reject questions that embed a required solution where alternatives remain material.
Track blueprint reuse, resolved uncertainty and execution defects; retire fields that do not change decisions.
Evidence/source hashes and dependency receipts stale slice eligibility.
Farm has no worker authority; release is separate and explicit.
Capability lookup is a mandatory blueprint input before proposing a new generator/system.

observability.human: Pulse/Funnel Fabric shows blueprint family, open questions, status, slice DAG and receipt state.
observability.physical: Future factory view may render blueprints as plans/folios; only released work appears active.

securityAuthority.planning: Blueprint Farm may create and revise planning artifacts.
securityAuthority.execution: Only an explicitly selected BF/child slice with Funnel authorization may execute.
securityAuthority.promotion: Ultra promotion is out of scope and separately gated.

rollback: BF-01 is additive JSON/index/test/library wiring. Removing the farm index and registrations leaves existing Funnel/Pulse/manufacturing systems unchanged; child blueprints remain ordinary repository artifacts.
